_comment: Tooltip has no `colors/tooltip` group in Figma V.7.1 and no component set either — but it IS drawn, as a plain FRAME on page `↳ tooltip ✅` (14964:58281). Colours here are authored against the semantic layer rather than mirrored, and the geometry is measured off that frame.
responsibility: Explain an element on hover or focus, without taking focus itself

tokens._comment: AUTHORED, NOT MIRRORED — see the file comment. Each maps to the semantic role whose value matches the Figma design's literal, so the alias chain still terminates in Figma.
tokens._source-trigger-icon-foreground: Figma paints the trigger icon with colors/icon/icon-fg-secondary (#262626). design.md models no `icon` colour group, so this points at text.secondary.default — same primitive (midnight.500), same value.

base._source-shadow: Nearest semantic elevation. The pre-token literal was `0 0 0 1px #0000000D, 0 1px 3px #0000001A`; elevation.card is `0 1px 3px #0000001A, 0 1px 2px #0000000F` — the 3px layer is identical, the 1px hairline ring layer is not modelled in design.md's shadow ladder.
base._source-max-width: storybook-local, no Figma token backs it — 326px is a fixed frame width on the tooltip content in Figma, and no semantic scale carries it.
base._source-min-width: storybook-local, no Figma token backs it — a legibility floor chosen in code, not a Figma measurement.
base._source-arrow: storybook-local, no Figma token backs them — the caret is a 16x8 vector in Figma, glyph geometry rather than spacing, so it is not expressed on the spacing ladder.
base._source-trigger-icon-size: storybook-local, no Figma token backs it — design.md's iconography.sizes are still 'tbd'; Figma binds the icons-size component at Size=24.

_source.shadow: Read off the frame: `0 0 0 1px #3F3F44 @5%` plus `0 1px 3px 0 #3F3F44 @15%`. The first is a hairline ring with no blur, not a shadow. #3F3F44 is in no palette in this system, and no elevation role carries this pair, so the value stands verbatim — Figma is the value authority.
_source.offset / min-width / trigger-icon-size: Library additions. Figma's frame states none of them: it draws one tooltip at one width with the arrow flush against the body.

_verified_from.node: 14964:58281 — FRAME `Tooltip` on page `↳ tooltip ✅`. Not a component and not a component set, which is why earlier notes said Figma had no tooltip. It has one; it was never componentised.
_verified_from.result: 326x98 = a 90px body plus an 8px arrow row. Body padding 12, radius 8, fill `colors/overlay/overlay-black-80%` — which is what `overlay-heavy` (#000000CC) already resolves to. Title 14/22 Medium and body 14/22 Regular, both `Color/Text/Text-Onbgcolor`. Arrow 16x8 in the same overlay fill. All match.

corrections.shadow: Was elevation.card — `0 1px 3px #0000001A, 0 1px 2px #0000000F`. Figma uses a different colour (#3F3F44, not black), different alphas (5% and 15%), and a 1px spread ring instead of the second shadow. Replaced with Figma's pair.

_figma_gaps.not-a-component: The tooltip is a loose FRAME. Nothing can instance it, so no page in the file can reuse it and any change has to be copied by hand. It should be a component set.
_figma_gaps.no-colour-group: There is no `colors/tooltip` variable group. The frame borrows `colors/overlay` and `Color/Text`, so the tokens here are authored against the semantic layer.
_figma_gaps.shadow-colour-off-palette: #3F3F44 appears nowhere else in the system. Kept because Figma is the value authority, but it looks like a default from a UI kit rather than a decision.

_figma_icons._comment: The icons Figma instantiates for this component, read 2026-08-20 by walking the instance tree and keeping every main component whose parent set is `icons`. check-figma-icons.py holds the files in `sources` to exactly this set — an extra icon fails as loudly as a missing one, because an extra is one nobody compared. Files not listed in `sources` carry payload a caller passes, not a choice the design makes.

nodes.note: Figma's tooltip draws no icon at all. The glyphs in Tooltip.stories.tsx are the demo payload a caller passes in, which is why the stories are not listed as a source: the component fixes nothing here, so there is nothing to hold it to.
